walkthrough:
State the definition of linear momentum for a particle:
$$p = mv$$

Substitute the given mass of particle $P$ ($m = 0.2\text{ kg}$) and its initial velocity ($v = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$):
$$p = 0.2 \times 2 = 0.4\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$$

hints: Apply the principle of conservation of linear momentum: total momentum before collision equals total momentum after.
Equate the initial momentum ($0.4\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$) to the sum of the final momenta: $0.2(0.3) + 0.5v$.
Solve the linear equation for the speed of $Q$, $v$.
walkthrough:
State the principle of conservation of linear momentum for an isolated two-particle system:
$$m_P u_P + m_Q u_Q = m_P v_P + m_Q v_Q$$

Substitute the values before and after collision:
From part (a), initial momentum is $0.4\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ (since particle $Q$ is initially at rest).
After collision, $P$ has mass $0.2\text{ kg}$ and speed $v_P = 0.3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in the same direction.
Particle $Q$ has mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ and final velocity $v$:
$$0.4 = 0.2 \times 0.3 + 0.5v$$
$$0.4 = 0.06 + 0.5v$$

Divide both sides by $0.5$:
$$v = \frac{0.34}{0.5} = 0.68\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
